title: Hosted 5xx trace-rescue and safe-retry suppressor for escalation storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers escalated after repeated 5xx/timeouts during tenant migration windows. Root cause traced to simultaneous KV-cache compaction and connection pool exhaustion which pushed many requests onto the slowpath; SDKs retried aggressively causing retry amplification and multi-tenant 5xx waves. This ticket implements a multi-part mitigation: (1) trace-forward 'rescue' header that short-circuits unsafe retries, (2) server-side safe-fastfail policy that returns a recoverable status (429 with Retry-After or 503 safe-fallback) when we detect queue + slowpath combos, and (3) per-tenant adaptive retry-suppressor that dampens client retries for a short hysteresis window while preserving idempotent semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Injected rescue header propagated end-to-end and honored by edge+runtime in rollout canary
Per-tenant retry-suppressor guards reduce observed retry amplification metric by >= 80% during simulated tenant surges
No customer-visible long tail 5xx wave in canary region for 48h under replayed traces
Automated chaos test added that triggers KV compaction + connection pool pressure and validates fastfail path
SDK guidance and header semantics documented in the API changelog
implementation_summary: Completed prototype in runtime that: 1) accepts X-Redwood-Rescue=<trace-id,ttl,mode> header and marks request as 'rescue-eligible'; 2) adds a lightweight admission controller that checks (queue_depth, kv_slowpath_flag, inflight_retries) and decides to fast-fail with 429/503 or allow pass-through; 3) implements a tenant-level in-memory token bucket that suppresses non-idempotent automatic retries for a configurable window; 4) exposes metrics: redis:tenant_retry_suppressions, runtime:rescue_handled_count, edge:fastfail_reasons. Patch: PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2804; edge changes PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/1421; SDK advisory draft https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/retry-guidance-draft
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Escalation triaged by oncall; initial spike captured — created ticket and assigned to reliability squad.
2025-02-15: HOTFIX-0 applied to edge to add temporary global retry-quarantine header for impacted customers (manual toggle). Early telemetry shows 30% drop in retries but 10% more 429s surfaced.

2025-02-18: Root cause narrowed to KV compaction + keepalive churn; reproduced in lab with tenant-replay harness. Determined need for server-side admission control rather than only client SDK changes.
2025-02-21: Implemented admission controller prototype and tenant token-bucket in runtime. Benchmarked latency impact (<1.2ms p50), rejection modes agreed in design review.
2025-02-25: PRs opened for runtime and edge. Integration tests added + new chaos test for kv-eviction storm. Human reviewer: Morgan Lee (SRE).
2025-03-01: Canary rollout started in us-west-2 with 5% traffic. Observed 85% reduction in retry amplification metric and stable p95 latency. Customer A confirmed reduction in errors.
2025-03-02: Rollback guard and toggle prepared. Internal SDK advisory drafted and sent to Developer Experience for publication. Seeking final signoff for region ramp.
Next: schedule global ramp, finish SDK minor version bump, and postmortem writeup
review_feedback: Morgan Lee (SRE): +1 on admission controller but asked to add circuit TTL and hard cap to avoid long-lived suppression windows
DevEx (J. Chen): Request to make rescue header optional-by-default and require SDK opt-in for early versions
Security (R. Gupta): reviewed header format, no sensitive data in trace header; recommended logging sampling to avoid PII leak
rollout_plan: Canary (us-west-2) 5% traffic — monitor retry_amplification, 5xx_rate, p95 latency for 48h
If stable, ramp to 25% after 24h and run full regression job for canary traces
45% ramp and SDK advisory release (minor) with guidance to set X-Redwood-Rescue for non-idempotent flows
Global ramp to 100% with post-rollout observability checks and stakeholder notifications
If any regression: immediate toggle-off via feature flag and incident runbook (see links)
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Tradeoff: fast-failing earlier surfaces errors to customers (429/503) instead of absorbing them — short-term UX degradation for fewer cascading outages.
Question: exact default suppression TTL (current prototype uses 6s with exponential backoff); ops requested lower default for high-QPS tenants.
Edge case: multi-hop requests (edge->router->runtime) must propagate rescue header reliably; need to verify across Dedicated/private control planes.
Follow-up: add permanent SDK changes to respect suppression header rather than temporary server-initiated behavior
postmortem_actions: Add tenant-surge synthetic tests to CI that run weekly
Provide SDK release and automated test that validates suppression header behavior
Instrument additional tracing to link client retry attempts to server-side suppression decisions
Schedule a cross-functional retro with customers affected and SRE/DevEx/Runtime teams
notes: This ticket spans Hosted primarily but has implications for Dedicated and Private (control-plane header propagation). Bridge ticket to Runtime ops created.
We intentionally return 429 with Retry-After for well-formed idempotent requests when possible; non-idempotent requests may receive 503 and an advisory to the app to retry via queued background job.
Operational knobs exposed as feature flags: suppression_ttl_seconds, admission_queue_depth_threshold, rescue_header_sampling_rate
